findings.title: enableSqlExpressions ignores the feature flag and always returns false
findings.body: The function computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)`, returns false if that is true, and otherwise also returns false. Every path returns false, so the flag has no effect. The inverted, redundant logic obscures that this is an unconditional kill switch. If someone later fixes the apparent inversion, or the flag is meant to re-enable the feature, the behaviour changes unpredictably. It also dereferences `h.features` for every SQL query, which panics if the reader was built with nil toggles. If the intent is to hard-disable SQL expressions, the case should return the error directly with a comment explaining why, and not consult a flag it then ignores.

findings.title: Misleading error and a still-advertised feature flag that now does nothing
findings.body: Users get `sqlExpressions is not implemented` even when they have explicitly enabled the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle. The PR description says the flag and its docs are intentionally left in place. Operators will therefore enable a documented flag and get a confusing error with no hint that the feature was deliberately disabled for security reasons. The message, and the flag's description or docs, should say the feature is disabled.

findings.title: Legacy UnmarshalSQLCommand path is disabled only as a side effect of the stub failing, with a misleading error
findings.body: Only the `ExpressionQueryReader` path gets an explicit guard. `UnmarshalSQLCommand` -> `NewSQLCommand` -> `sql.TablesList` is not gated. It is blocked only because the stub `DB.RunCommands` returns an error. `NewSQLCommand` then logs a warning about an invalid sql query and returns a BadRequest `sql-invalid-sql` / 'error reading SQL command'. Users see a bad-query error instead of 'feature disabled', and the logs say the SQL was invalid. The security posture also depends on the stub never being implemented or partially restored. A single explicit gate inside `NewSQLCommand` / `Execute` would be more robust.

findings.title: Dead DuckDB-specific code left behind
findings.body: `TablesList` still builds a DuckDB `json_serialize_sql` command and parses its JSON AST, and the variable is still named `duckDB`. Against the stub it always returns an error. `tablesFromAST` and its helpers are therefore unreachable from production code. This leftover code makes the disabling look incomplete and invites someone to wire a real backend back in without a security review. It should be removed or clearly marked as disabled.

findings.title: No tests cover the new disabled behaviour; existing SQL tests are not updated
findings.body: This security fix adds no test asserting that a `sql` query type is rejected by `ReadQuery`. It also adds none asserting that `NewSQLCommand`/`Execute` fail with the stub. Existing tests that exercise `sql.TablesList` or SQL command execution against a real DuckDB are not touched in this diff. They will either fail or silently test nothing now that `TablesList` and `QueryFramesInto` always return 'not implemented'. A regression test is especially valuable here so the guard is not accidentally removed.
